Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verses 1–3:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Ha-Mim. By the Clear Book, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an, that you may understand.﴾

We have already explained in what has passed His words ﴿Ha-Mim﴾, with what suffices so that it need not be repeated in this place.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And by the Clear Book﴾

It is an oath by God, exalted is He, swearing by this Book which He sent down to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). He says: ﴿And by the Clear Book﴾, for whoever reflects upon it and contemplates its lessons and admonitions, it guides him, leads him to right direction, and shows him its proofs of its truth, and that it is a revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy, not a fabrication by Muhammad (ﷺ) nor an invention of anyone. ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾ means: We sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an, in the language of the Arabs, since you, O people addressed by it, the kin of Muhammad (ﷺ), are Arabs. ﴿That you may understand﴾ means: its meanings and the admonitions contained in it. He did not send it down in the language of the non-Arabs (ʿajam), making it non-Arabic, so that you would say, "We are Arabs, and this is a non-Arabic speech whose meanings we do not comprehend."

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Ha-Mim. And by the Clear Book﴾: it is this clear Book.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Ha-Mim. And by the Clear Book﴾: "Clear" — by God's blessing, His guidance and His right direction.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted, wise.﴾

Allah, dhikruhu (His remembrance is exalted), says: Indeed this Book is the origin of the Book from which this Book was copied with Us, ʿaliyy (exalted): meaning, possessing height and elevated rank; ḥakīm (wise): its verses have been made firm (uḥkimat), then detailed (fuṣṣilat), so it possesses wisdom.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said so:

⁕ Yaʿqub narrated to me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Hisham al-Dastawa'i, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, who said: ʿUrwah ibn ʿAmir related to us, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbas say: The first thing Allah created was the pen, and He commanded it to write what He wished to create. He said: The Book was with Him. He said: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted, wise.﴾ Meaning: the Qur'an is in the Mother of the Book, which is with Allah, from which it was copied.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, he said: Ibn Idris related to us, he said: I heard my father, from ʿAtiyyah ibn Saʿd, regarding the words of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted, wise.﴾ Meaning: the Qur'an is in the Mother of the Book, which is with Allah, from which it was copied.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, he said: Ibn Idris related to us, he said: I heard Malik narrate from ʿImran, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book with Us﴾ he said: The Mother of the Book is the Qur'an.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book with Us﴾ he said: The Mother of the Book: the origin of the Book and its whole.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book﴾: meaning the totality of the Book, i.e., the origin of the Book.

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book﴾ he says: in the Book that is with Allah in origin.

* *

As for His words: ﴿with Us, exalted, wise﴾

We have already mentioned its meaning.

The people of ta'wil have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said so:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿with Us, exalted, wise﴾ he informs about His station, His favour and His nobility.

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Shall We withhold the Reminder from you, turning away from you, because you are a people who transgress?﴾ (43:5)

The people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: its meaning is: Shall We turn away from you and leave you, O polytheists, in what you suppose, so that We do not remind you of Our punishment because you are a people who associate others with God.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Shall We withhold the Reminder from you, turning away?﴾ He said: You deny the Qur'an, and then you are not punished for it.

- Muhammad ibn Amara related to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, his words: ﴿Shall We withhold the Reminder from you, turning away?﴾ He said: with the punishment.

- Muhammad related to me, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Shall We withhold the Reminder from you, turning away?﴾ He said: Shall We withhold the punishment from you.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his words: ﴿Shall We withhold the Reminder from you, turning away, because you are a people who transgress?﴾ He says: Do you suppose that We will overlook you while you have not done what you were commanded?

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Shall We cease reminding you with this Qur'an and not remind you of it, because you are a people who transgress?

Those who said this:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: ﴿Shall We withhold the Reminder from you, turning away, because you are a people who transgress?﴾ He said: That is, polytheists. By God, if this Qur'an had been lifted when the first of this community rejected it, they would have been destroyed. He called them to it for twenty years, or whatever God willed of that.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿Shall We withhold the Reminder from you, turning away?﴾ He said: If this community had not believed, the Reminder would have been withheld from them, turning away; he said: The Reminder is what was revealed to them of what God commanded them and forbade them, turning away, not mentioning any of it to you.

The more correct of the two interpretations, in our view, is the one who interpreted it as: Shall We withhold the punishment from you, leaving you and turning away from you, because you are a people who do not believe in your Lord.

We said that this is the more fitting of the two interpretations for the verse, because God, blessed and exalted, follows this with His report about the earlier nations before the nations He threatened with this verse, in their denial of their messengers, and the vengeance He inflicted upon them. In this is evidence that His words: ﴿Shall We withhold the Reminder from you, turning away?﴾ are a threat from Him to those addressed by it from among the polytheists, since they followed, in denying what their messenger brought them from God, the course of those who passed before them.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Kufa recited ﴿in kuntum﴾ with a kasra on the alif of "in," meaning: Shall We withhold the Reminder from you, turning away, since you are a people who transgress. Some readers of Mecca and Kufa and the majority of the readers of Basra recited ﴿an kuntum﴾ with a fatha on the alif of "an," meaning: because you are a people who transgress.

The grammarians differed regarding the reason for the fatha on the alif of "an" in this position. Some grammarians of Basra said: it was given a fatha because the meaning of the speech is: because you were. Some grammarians of Kufa said: whoever gave it a fatha intended something past, so he said: You say in speech: "I came to you because you deprived me" (atayta an harramtani), meaning: since you deprived me; and it takes a kasra when you intend: "I came to you if you deprive me" (atayta in tuharrimani). Similar to it is: ﴿and let not the hatred of a people lead you to transgress, because they barred you﴾ (la yajrimannakum shana'an qawmin an sadduukum), with a kasra and a fatha. ...

[Translator's note omitted: the following passage is the poetic illustration and commentary as given in the source.]

The poet's line (Farazdaq): "Do you grieve that the ears of Qutayba were cut off openly, and you did not grieve for the killing of Ibn Khazim?" and the line of Kuthayyir 'Azza: "Do you grieve that the departing companions have gone, and the cord of Safa from 'Azza is broken?" — he said: In each of the two lines there is what is in the other of fatha and kasra.

The correct statement on this matter, in our view, is that kasra and fatha on the alif in this position are two well-known recitations among the readers of the cities, both sound in meaning; whichever reader recites either is correct. This is because when the Arabs place "an" before a future verb with the sense of a condition, they sometimes give its alif a kasra, making it purely conditional, and they say: "I will stand if I stand"; and sometimes they give it a fatha while intending that meaning, saying: "I will stand because I stood," by interpretation, "because I stood." When the verb preceding it is past, they say only with a fatha on the alif of "an," saying: "I stood because I stood," and with this the revelation came, and the poetry of poets followed suit.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verses 6–8:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿How many a prophet did We send among the earlier peoples? (6) And no prophet came to them but that they used to mock him.﴾ (7)

His saying, Exalted is His remembrance: ﴿How many a prophet did We send among the earlier peoples?﴾ O Muhammad, among the earlier generations who passed before your generation in which you were sent, just as We sent you among your people, the Quraysh. ﴿And no prophet came to them but that they used to mock him.﴾ That is, no prophet came to one of those earlier generations and nations of the ancients, calling them to guidance and the path of truth, except that those people to whom he came mocked their prophet whom He had sent to them, mocking them, just as your people mock you, O Muhammad. That is to say: do not let what your people do to you weigh heavily upon you, nor let it grieve you, for in their mockery of you they have only followed the course of their predecessors and the methods of their leaders from the past who disbelieved in God.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So We destroyed those who were stronger than them in might, and the example of the earlier peoples has passed on.﴾ (8)

His saying, Exalted is His remembrance: So We destroyed those mockers of their prophets who were stronger than these in might when they struck, for they could not overpower Us by their strength and the severity of their might, nor were they able to resist Our punishment when it came upon them. Hence those who are weaker than them in strength are even less able to resist Our vengeance when it descends upon them. He, glorified is His praise, says: And there has passed on for these polytheists who mock you, O Muhammad, and for those before them of their kind, the example of Our dealings with the like of them among the deniers of Our messengers whom We destroyed. That is to say: let those who mock you, O Muhammad, expect a punishment from Us like that which We inflicted upon those who persisted in denying you.

And the people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and the example of the earlier peoples has passed on﴾, he said: the punishment of the earlier peoples.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿the example of the earlier peoples﴾, he said: their custom (sunnah).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 11–12:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And He who sends down water from the sky in a measure, and We revive therewith a dead land. Thus you will be brought forth﴾ (11), ﴿And He who created all the pairs and made for you of the ships and cattle that you ride﴾ (12).

His saying, may He be mentioned, ﴿And He who sends down water from the sky in a measure﴾ means: what He, may His majesty be praised, sends down of rain from the sky in a measure, that is, in the amount of your need for it. So He did not make it like the flood, which would be a punishment like that sent down upon the people of Noah, nor did He make it so little that plants and crops could not grow from its scarcity; rather He made it a life-giving rain, reviving the dead earth. ﴿So We revived therewith a dead town﴾ means: He, may His majesty be praised, says: So We brought to life with it a town of yours, dead, meaning barren, with no plants or crops in it, its traces worn away by drought and rotted by dryness. ﴿Thus you will be brought forth﴾ means: may He be mentioned, says: just as We brought forth plants and crops from this dead town after its barrenness and dryness by this water We sent down from the sky, so too, O people, you will be brought forth after your annihilation and your returning to the earth as crumbled remains, by the water He sends down to it to give you life after your death, living as you were in your state before your death.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And He who sends down water from the sky in a measure﴾ ... the verse: just as Allah revived this dead land by this water, so you will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection.

It was said: "We revived it therewith" (anshharna), because its meaning is "We gave life with it." Had the land been described as having been given life, it would be said: "The land was made to spread out (nushirat)," as al-A'sha said:

"Until people say, seeing it: 'How wondrous, the dead one who rises!'" [The verse is by al-A'sha Maymun ibn Qays, from a qasidah in which he satirizes Alqamah ibn Ulathah and praises Amir ibn al-Tufayl, in the contest of boasting between them (his Diwan, 139). Alqamah ibn Ulathah was a Companion who came to the Prophet (ﷺ) as an old man, and embraced Islam and pledged allegiance. The verse is among the evidences cited by Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 220-1), at the saying of the Exalted in Surah al-Zukhruf: "So We revived therewith a dead town," where he said: "We gave life." And "the land was nushirat" means it came to life. Al-A'sha said: "Until people say... " the verse. In (Lisan al-'Arab, root nashara): "God nashara the dead, nashran and nushuran, and anshahu, gave him life, so he rose (nashara), al-A'sha said: 'Until people say...' the verse." End.]

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And He who created all the pairs﴾

His saying, may He be mentioned: "And He who created every thing in pairs", that is, He created males from females and females from males as pairs. ﴿And made for you of the ships﴾, which are the vessels, ﴿and cattle﴾, which are the beasts, ﴿that you ride﴾ means: He made for you of the ships what you ride on the seas to wherever you intend and aim to travel for your livelihood and your needs, and of the cattle what you ride on land to whatever lands you wish, such as camels, horses, mules and donkeys.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 11–12:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And He who sends down water from the sky in a measure, and We revive therewith a dead land. Thus you will be brought forth﴾ (11), ﴿And He who created all the pairs and made for you of the ships and cattle that you ride﴾ (12).

His saying, may He be mentioned, ﴿And He who sends down water from the sky in a measure﴾ means: what He, may His majesty be praised, sends down of rain from the sky in a measure, that is, in the amount of your need for it. So He did not make it like the flood, which would be a punishment like that sent down upon the people of Noah, nor did He make it so little that plants and crops could not grow from its scarcity; rather He made it a life-giving rain, reviving the dead earth. ﴿So We revived therewith a dead town﴾ means: He, may His majesty be praised, says: So We brought to life with it a town of yours, dead, meaning barren, with no plants or crops in it, its traces worn away by drought and rotted by dryness. ﴿Thus you will be brought forth﴾ means: may He be mentioned, says: just as We brought forth plants and crops from this dead town after its barrenness and dryness by this water We sent down from the sky, so too, O people, you will be brought forth after your annihilation and your returning to the earth as crumbled remains, by the water He sends down to it to give you life after your death, living as you were in your state before your death.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And He who sends down water from the sky in a measure﴾ ... the verse: just as Allah revived this dead land by this water, so you will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection.

It was said: "We revived it therewith" (anshharna), because its meaning is "We gave life with it." Had the land been described as having been given life, it would be said: "The land was made to spread out (nushirat)," as al-A'sha said:

"Until people say, seeing it: 'How wondrous, the dead one who rises!'" [The verse is by al-A'sha Maymun ibn Qays, from a qasidah in which he satirizes Alqamah ibn Ulathah and praises Amir ibn al-Tufayl, in the contest of boasting between them (his Diwan, 139). Alqamah ibn Ulathah was a Companion who came to the Prophet (ﷺ) as an old man, and embraced Islam and pledged allegiance. The verse is among the evidences cited by Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 220-1), at the saying of the Exalted in Surah al-Zukhruf: "So We revived therewith a dead town," where he said: "We gave life." And "the land was nushirat" means it came to life. Al-A'sha said: "Until people say... " the verse. In (Lisan al-'Arab, root nashara): "God nashara the dead, nashran and nushuran, and anshahu, gave him life, so he rose (nashara), al-A'sha said: 'Until people say...' the verse." End.]

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And He who created all the pairs﴾

His saying, may He be mentioned: "And He who created every thing in pairs", that is, He created males from females and females from males as pairs. ﴿And made for you of the ships﴾, which are the vessels, ﴿and cattle﴾, which are the beasts, ﴿that you ride﴾ means: He made for you of the ships what you ride on the seas to wherever you intend and aim to travel for your livelihood and your needs, and of the cattle what you ride on land to whatever lands you wish, such as camels, horses, mules and donkeys.

The Interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿That you may sit firmly upon their backs, then remember the favour of your Lord when you are settled upon them, and say: Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, and we could not have subdued them by ourselves. And indeed to our Lord we are returning﴾ (43:13–14)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: So that you may sit firmly upon the backs of what you ride.

The grammarians of Arabic differed over the reason the pronoun in His words ﴿عَلَى ظُهُورِهِ﴾ ("upon its backs") is singular ("its" rather than "their"). Some of the grammarians of Basra said: its masculine form refers to what you ride, and what you ride is not masculine, as one says: "Among the women there is someone (min al-nisa' man) who agrees with you and pleases you," and the livestock (al-an'am) are sometimes treated as masculine and sometimes as feminine. He has said elsewhere: ﴿مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ﴾ ("of what is in its bellies"), and elsewhere He said: ﴿بُطُونِهَا﴾ ("their bellies"). Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: the word "backs" (zuhur) was made dependent on a singular noun, because that singular noun carries the meaning of a plural, in the manner of "al-jund" (the army) and "al-jaysh" (the host). He said: If it is said, "Why not say: to sit firmly upon its back, making 'back' singular since you attached it to a singular?" I reply: The singular there carries the meaning of the plural, so they returned "backs" to the sense and did not say "its back," which would be like a singular whose meaning and form are both singular. Likewise you say: "The number of the army's women has increased," and "The army raised his eye" and did not say "its eye." He said: Likewise, every noun that you attach to a descriptive noun, make it plural; and when you attach to it a noun having the sense of a verb, it is permissible to make it plural or singular, as in your saying: "The troop raised its voice (sawtahu)," and "their voices (aswatuhu) are better." This is permissible because the verb has no distinct form for the dual other than the form for the singular.

Another of them said: It was said, "to sit firmly upon its back," because it is a description of the ship; but he made the pronoun singular, because the ship is understood as a collective, so he made "backs" plural and the pronoun singular, because the verbs of each collective, when understood as plural, may be singular or plural, as in "the army is defeated" and "they are defeated." When nouns of this kind occur, they follow the forms of the nouns and nothing else, so you say, "The army are men," and therefore "backs" is plural and the pronoun singular. Had it been like "voice" and similar words, one would say, "The army raised his voice (rafa'a sawtahu)" and "their voices (aswatuhu)."

* *

His words: ﴿Then remember the favour of your Lord﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Then remember the favour of your Lord which He has bestowed upon you by subjecting these to you as vehicles on land and sea, ﴿when you are settled upon them﴾, so that you magnify and glorify Him, and say, declaring Allah free of what the polytheists attribute to Him and of associating with Him in worship idols and images, of these ships and livestock which we have mounted: ﴿Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, and we could not have subdued them by ourselves﴾.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Abu Kurayb and Ubayd ibn Isma'il al-Hubari related to us, they said: al-Muharibi related to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu Hashim, from Abu Mijlaz, who said: I rode an animal and said: ﴿Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, and we could not have subdued them by ourselves﴾. A man from the people of the household heard me. Abu Kurayb and al-Hubari said: al-Muharibi said: I heard Sufyan say: He was al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both. He said: "Is this how you were commanded?" I said: "How should I say it?" He said: "Say: Praise be to Allah who guided us to Islam; Praise be to Allah who favoured us with Muhammad (ﷺ); Praise be to Allah who placed us in the best nation brought forth for mankind." Then you have mentioned great blessings, after which say: ﴿Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, and we could not have subdued them by ourselves, and indeed to our Lord we are returning﴾.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Hashim, from Abu Mijlaz, that al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, saw a man who had mounted an animal, and said: "Praise be to Allah who has subjected this to us," then he mentioned something similar.

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿That you may sit firmly upon their backs, then remember the favour of your Lord when you are settled upon them﴾: He teaches you what to say when you board the ship: you say, ﴿In the name of Allah be its course and its mooring; indeed my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful﴾; and when you ride camels you say: ﴿Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, and we could not have subdued them by ourselves, and indeed to our Lord we are returning﴾. And He teaches you what to say when you alight from the ships and the livestock together: you say, "O Allah, cause us to alight at a blessed place, and You are the best of those who cause to alight."

- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, that when he rode he would say: "O Allah, this is from Your bounty and grace," then say: ﴿Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, and we could not have subdued them by ourselves, and indeed to our Lord we are returning﴾.

* *

His words: ﴿and we could not have subdued them by ourselves﴾

That is: we were not capable of them and could not control them, from their saying, "I have made myself a match for this" (aqranta li-hadha) when one becomes a match for it and is able to master it; and "So-and-so is a match for so-and-so" means he is able to control him and is capable of him.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- 'Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and we could not have subdued them by ourselves﴾: he says, "capable of them."

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿matching (muqrinin)﴾, he said: the camels, the horses, the mules and the donkeys.

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and we could not have subdued them by ourselves﴾, that is, "capable of them; no, by Allah, neither in power nor in strength."

- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, his words: ﴿and we could not have subdued them by ourselves﴾, he said: "in strength."

- Muhammad related to us, he said: Ahmad related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and we could not have subdued them by ourselves﴾, he said: "capable of them."

- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the words of Allah, Majestic is His praise: ﴿Glory be to Him who has subjected these to us, and we could not have subdued them by ourselves﴾, he said: "We are not capable of them; we cannot manage them except through You. Were it not for You, we would not have been strong enough for them, nor able to manage them."

His words: ﴿And indeed to our Lord we are returning﴾

He, exalted is His praise, says: And let them also say: And indeed to our Lord, after our death, we are those who will surely go back and return to Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 15–17:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion of His servants. Indeed, mankind is a manifest ingrate.﴾ (15) ﴿Or has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you?﴾ (16) ﴿And when one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief.﴾ (17)

God, His remembrance is exalted, says: These polytheists have assigned to God a share of His creation, and that is their saying regarding the angels: they are the daughters of God.

Those who held this view among the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion of His servants﴾. He said: a child, and daughters from among the angels.

Muhammad told us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion of His servants﴾. He said: the daughters.

Others said: by "portion" (juz') here is meant: equal (adl).

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion of His servants﴾: that is, an equal.

Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion of His servants﴾: that is, an equal.

We chose the view we have chosen in interpreting this only because God, His praise is exalted, followed that with His saying: ﴿Or has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you?﴾, as a rebuke to them for their saying. It is therefore known that His rebuke of them for this is only concerning what He reported of their statement, what they said about attributing daughters to God, His praise is exalted.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is a manifest ingrate.﴾

God, His remembrance is exalted, says: Indeed, mankind is one who clearly denies the blessings of his Lord which He has bestowed upon him: that is, his ingratitude for His blessings upon him is evident to whoever reflects with the thought of his heart and contemplates his condition.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Or has He taken daughters from what He creates﴾

His praise is exalted, rebuking these polytheists who described Him as having the angels as His daughters, says: Has your Lord, O ignorant ones, taken daughters from what He creates, while you do not approve for yourselves [such], and has chosen sons for you? That is: and has purified you with sons, giving them to you. ﴿And when one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness﴾ God, His remembrance is exalted, says: And when one of these polytheists who assign to God a portion of His servants is given good news of what he has likened to the Most Merciful, that is: of what he has made a likeness for God, thus comparing Him, and that is what he described Him with, namely that He has daughters.

As:

Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness﴾. He said: a child.

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness": of what he has made for God.

* *

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿and he suppresses grief﴾: that is, sorrowful.

He said: a child.

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness": of what he has made for God.

* *

And His saying: ﴿his face becomes dark﴾

God, His remembrance is exalted, says: the face of this one who was given good news of what he has likened to the Most Merciful, namely daughters, became dark from the evil of what he was given news of. ﴿and he suppresses grief﴾ means: and he is sorrowful.

As:

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿and he suppresses grief﴾: that is, sorrowful.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 15–17:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion of His servants. Indeed, mankind is a manifest ingrate.﴾ (15) ﴿Or has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you?﴾ (16) ﴿And when one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief.﴾ (17)

God, His remembrance is exalted, says: These polytheists have assigned to God a share of His creation, and that is their saying regarding the angels: they are the daughters of God.

Those who held this view among the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion of His servants﴾. He said: a child, and daughters from among the angels.

Muhammad told us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion of His servants﴾. He said: the daughters.

Others said: by "portion" (juz') here is meant: equal (adl).

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion of His servants﴾: that is, an equal.

Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion of His servants﴾: that is, an equal.

We chose the view we have chosen in interpreting this only because God, His praise is exalted, followed that with His saying: ﴿Or has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you?﴾, as a rebuke to them for their saying. It is therefore known that His rebuke of them for this is only concerning what He reported of their statement, what they said about attributing daughters to God, His praise is exalted.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is a manifest ingrate.﴾

God, His remembrance is exalted, says: Indeed, mankind is one who clearly denies the blessings of his Lord which He has bestowed upon him: that is, his ingratitude for His blessings upon him is evident to whoever reflects with the thought of his heart and contemplates his condition.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Or has He taken daughters from what He creates﴾

His praise is exalted, rebuking these polytheists who described Him as having the angels as His daughters, says: Has your Lord, O ignorant ones, taken daughters from what He creates, while you do not approve for yourselves [such], and has chosen sons for you? That is: and has purified you with sons, giving them to you. ﴿And when one of them is given good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness﴾ God, His remembrance is exalted, says: And when one of these polytheists who assign to God a portion of His servants is given good news of what he has likened to the Most Merciful, that is: of what he has made a likeness for God, thus comparing Him, and that is what he described Him with, namely that He has daughters.

As:

Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness﴾. He said: a child.

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness": of what he has made for God.

* *

And His saying: ﴿his face becomes dark﴾

God, His remembrance is exalted, says: the face of this one who was given good news of what he has likened to the Most Merciful, namely daughters, became dark from the evil of what he was given news of. ﴿and he suppresses grief﴾ means: and he is sorrowful.

As:

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿and he suppresses grief﴾: that is, sorrowful.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 18:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is one who is brought up among ornaments, and who, in a dispute, is not clear [in expression]?﴾ (43:18)

He, the Exalted, says: Or is one who grows up adorned with ornaments, ﴿and who, in dispute﴾ — meaning: while he is in a dispute with whoever disputes with him — ﴿is not clear﴾, and cannot put forward proof and argument against his opponent, because of his weakness and feebleness. Yet you have made him a part of God's creation and claimed that he is His portion from them. In the speech there is an omitted element, dispensed with by the indication of what has been mentioned, which is what I have described.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the one meant by His saying: ﴿Or is one who is brought up among ornaments, and who, in dispute, is not clear?﴾ Some of them said: it refers to young women and women.

Mention of those who said this:

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Or is one who is brought up among ornaments, and who, in dispute, is not clear?﴾ He said: it means the woman.

• Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Alqamah, from Murthid, from Mujahid, who said: [Concession] was granted to women regarding silk and gold, and he recited: ﴿Or is one who is brought up among ornaments, and who, in dispute, is not clear?﴾ He said: it means the woman.

• Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Or is one who is brought up among ornaments, and who, in dispute, is not clear?﴾ He said: the young women, whom you have made to the Merciful as offspring. How do you judge?

• Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Or is one who is brought up among ornaments, and who, in dispute, is not clear?﴾ He said: the young women, whom he disparages by this, unclear because of their weakness.

• Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Or is one who is brought up among ornaments?﴾ He says: they attributed daughters to Him, while when one of them is given the good news of them, his face darkens and he is filled with suppressed grief. He said: As for His saying: ﴿and who, in dispute, is not clear﴾, he says: a woman rarely speaks when she wishes to make her argument except that she ends up speaking the argument against herself.

• Muhammad related to us, he said: Ahmad related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Or is one who is brought up among ornaments, and who, in dispute, is not clear?﴾ He said: the women.

Others said: it means their idols which they worshipped besides God.

Mention of those who said this:

• Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Or is one who is brought up among ornaments?﴾ ... the verse. He said: these are their images which they strike from silver and gold, which they worship; they are the ones who made them, struck them from that ornament, and then worshipped them. ﴿And who, in dispute, is not clear﴾ — he said: it does not speak. And he recited: ﴿then behold, he is an open adversary﴾.

The more correct of the two opinions regarding this, in our view, is the opinion of the one who said: it refers to young women and women, because this comes directly after God's report of the polytheists' attributing to Him what they dislike for themselves, namely daughters, and their little knowledge of His right, and their describing Him with attributes of ornament and stinginess, while He is their Creator, their Owner, their Provider, and the One who bestowed upon them the blessings which He enumerated at the beginning of this surah, which they do not accept for themselves. Thus, following the speech that is closest in parallel to it is more fitting and more appropriate than following what has no mention preceding it.

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His saying: ﴿Or is one who is brought up among ornaments?﴾ The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some of the Meccans and Kufans, recited "أوْ مَنْ يَنْشَأُ" with a fatha on the ya' and without shadda, from نَشَأَ yansha'u. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited ﴿يُنَشَّأُ﴾ with a damma on the ya' and a shadda on the shin, from نَشَّأْتُهُ fa-huwa yunasha'u. The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is to say: they are two well-known recitations among the recitations of the regions, close in meaning, because the one made to grow (al-munasha') is from al-insha' (causing to grow), and the one who grows (al-nashi') is one who has grown up; so whichever of the two a reader recites, he is correct. It has been mentioned that in the recitation of Abdullah it is: "أوَ مَنْ لا يُنشَّأُ إلا فِي الحلْية"; and regarding "man" there are aspects of i'rab: the nominative (raf') as a resumption (isti'naf), and the accusative (nasb) by supposing a verb, as if it were said: "Or is one who grows up in ornaments, they make for God daughters?" The accusative may also be permitted, by way of returning to His saying: "Has He taken what He creates as daughters, or one who grows up in ornaments?", so that "man" refers back to "banat" (daughters); and the genitive (khafd) by way of returning to the "ma" in His saying: ﴿when one of them is given the good news of what he has attributed to the Most Merciful as a likeness﴾.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 19:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: These polytheists who associate others with God have made His angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, [into females].

The reciters differed over the recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as "alladhina hum 'inda al-Rahman" with the letter nun, as if they interpreted it according to the words of God, may His praise be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord are not too proud [to worship Him]﴾. So the meaning of the statement according to this recitation is: "And they made the angels of God, who are with Him, glorifying Him and sanctifying Him, females," and they said: "They are the daughters of God," out of ignorance of the right of God and audacity on their part in speaking falsehood and vanity. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it as ﴿and they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females﴾, in the sense of the plural of "abd" (servant). So the meaning of the statement according to the recitation of these reciters is: "And they made the angels of God, who are His creation and servants, daughters of God," and so they attributed femininity to them by describing them as females.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that both are well-known recitations among the recitation of the regional centres, and both are sound in meaning. Whichever of them the reader recites is correct, because the angels are servants of God and with Him.

They also differed over the recitation of His saying: ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾ Some of the reciters of Medina read it as "ashahadu khalqahum" with a damma on the alif, in the passive form (the subject not named), meaning: "Did God make these polytheists, who made the angels of God females, witness the creation of His angels who are with Him, so that they knew what they are and that they are females, and therefore described them as such, because of their knowledge of them and their seeing them?" Then this was referred back to the passive form.

It was also recited with a fatha on the alif, meaning: "Did they themselves witness that, so that they knew it?" The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that both are well-known recitations, and whichever the reader recites is correct.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Their testimony will be recorded﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: The testimony of these speakers, who say "The angels are daughters of God," will be recorded in this world against them for what they testified to, and they will be questioned in the Hereafter about that testimony, to bring proof of its truth, and they will not find any way to that.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have no knowledge of that; they only guess.﴾ ﴿Or have We given them a Book before this, so that they hold fast to it?﴾

He, exalted is He, says: These polytheists of Quraysh said: "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped our idols, which we worship besides Him." And [they said] that He had not sent a punishment upon us for our worship of them because He was pleased with us for worshipping them.

As related to us:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them﴾ [meaning] the idols: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says it. ﴿They have no knowledge of that﴾ means: they have no knowledge of the reality of what they say in this regard; rather, they say it as conjecture and falsehood, for they have no information from Me about it, nor any proof. They say it only as supposition and assumption. ﴿They only guess﴾ means: they are only fabricators of this statement which they made, namely their saying ﴿If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them﴾.

Mujahid used to say, regarding the interpretation of that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to us, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿they only guess﴾: they do not know the power of Allah to do that.

* *

As for His words ﴿Or have We given them a Book before this﴾:

He, exalted is He, says: Have We given these fabricators, who say "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped the deities," a Book confirming the reality of what they say in this regard, before this Qur'an which We have sent down to you, O Muhammad? ﴿So they hold fast to it﴾ means: do they hold fast to that Book which came to them from Me before this Qur'an, acting by it, adhering to what is in it, and using it as proof against you?

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have no knowledge of that; they only guess.﴾ ﴿Or have We given them a Book before this, so that they hold fast to it?﴾

He, exalted is He, says: These polytheists of Quraysh said: "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped our idols, which we worship besides Him." And [they said] that He had not sent a punishment upon us for our worship of them because He was pleased with us for worshipping them.

As related to us:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them﴾ [meaning] the idols: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says it. ﴿They have no knowledge of that﴾ means: they have no knowledge of the reality of what they say in this regard; rather, they say it as conjecture and falsehood, for they have no information from Me about it, nor any proof. They say it only as supposition and assumption. ﴿They only guess﴾ means: they are only fabricators of this statement which they made, namely their saying ﴿If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them﴾.

Mujahid used to say, regarding the interpretation of that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to us, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿they only guess﴾: they do not know the power of Allah to do that.

* *

As for His words ﴿Or have We given them a Book before this﴾:

He, exalted is He, says: Have We given these fabricators, who say "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped the deities," a Book confirming the reality of what they say in this regard, before this Qur'an which We have sent down to you, O Muhammad? ﴿So they hold fast to it﴾ means: do they hold fast to that Book which came to them from Me before this Qur'an, acting by it, adhering to what is in it, and using it as proof against you?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 22:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nay, but they say: "We found our fathers following a religion, and we are guided upon their footsteps."﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: We did not give these speakers [a book] that says, "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped these idols," by a command to worship them, [a book] from Us. Rather, they said: "We found our fathers who were before us worshipping them, so we worship them as they used to worship them." By His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿Nay, but we found our fathers following a religion [ummah]﴾ [[Recitation: "Nay, but they say: We found our fathers upon a community (ummah)."]], meaning: we found our fathers upon a religion and a creed, and that is their worship of idols.

Similar to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿upon a religion [ummah]﴾: a creed (milla).

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿We found our fathers upon a religion [ummah]﴾, he said: "We found our fathers upon a religion."

- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿We found our fathers upon a religion [ummah]﴾, he said: The polytheists of Quraysh indeed said this: "We found our fathers upon a religion."

- Muhammad told us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, ﴿They say: We found our fathers upon a religion [ummah]﴾, he said: upon a religion.

The reciters differed regarding the reading of His saying: ﴿upon a community [ummah]﴾. The majority of the reciters of the regional centres read ﴿ummah﴾ with a damma on the alif, in the meaning described: religion, creed and path. It is related from Mujahid and 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz that they read it as "imma" with a kasra on the alif. Its meaning when the alif is given a kasra has been differed over. Some of them directed its interpretation, when it is kasred, to mean the path (al-tariqa), and that it is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "amamtu al-qawm fa-ana u'ummuhum imma" (I led the people, and I lead them). It is related from the Arabs by hearing: "How good is his 'amma (manner of turban), his imma and his jilsa (manner of sitting)" when it is a verbal noun. Some of them directed it, when its alif is kasred, to mean the imma that signifies blessing and dominion, as 'Adi ibn Zayd said: "Then after success and dominion and imma, the graves have covered them there." [[The line is by 'Adi ibn Zayd al-'Ibadi (Lisan: amam), and it is among the evidences of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, at His saying (Indeed we found our fathers upon a community) (folio 294), where he said: The reciters read it with a damma on the alif of "ummah", and Mujahid and 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz gave it a kasra. It seems that imma means the path, the verbal noun of "amamtu al-qawm"; for the Arabs say: "How good is his imma, his 'amma and his jilsa," when it is a verbal noun. Ummah also means dominion and blessing. 'Adi said: "Thumma ba'da al-falah..." the line. So it seems he meant the leadership of dominion and its blessing. End. In Lisan: "ummah" (with damma) and with kasra mean religion. "Imma" (with kasra) is a dialectal form of "ummah" (with damma), and it means path and religion. End.]]

And he said: he meant the leadership of dominion and its blessing. Some of them said: "al-umma with damma and al-imma with kasra have one meaning."

The correct reading in this matter, which I do not permit otherwise, is the damma on the alif, by the consensus of the authoritative reciters of the regional centres upon it. As for those who gave it a kasra, I do not see that they intended by the kasra anything but the meaning of path and method, as we mentioned before, not blessing and dominion, because there is no sense in saying: "We found our fathers upon a blessing, and we are followers of them in that," since following is only in creeds and religions and what resembles them, not in dominion and blessing, for following in dominion is not a matter that reaches everyone who wants it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And we are guided upon their footsteps﴾

He says: And we are guided upon the footsteps of our fathers in what they were upon of their religion, meaning: we are followers of them upon their method.

As related:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And we are guided upon their footsteps﴾, he said: "And we are upon their religion."

- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And we are guided upon their footsteps﴾, he said: "And we are their followers in that."

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We did not send before you any warner into a town but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps."﴾ (43:23)

His exalted remembrance says: Thus, just as these polytheists of Quraysh did, those before them among the people of disbelief in Allah did the same, and they said the same as their words. We did not send before you, O Muhammad, into any town, meaning to its people, messengers to warn them of Our punishment for their disbelief in Us, so they warned them and cautioned them of Our wrath and the descent of Our punishment upon them. ﴿But its affluent ones said﴾, and they are their leaders and their elders.

As related:

* Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿But its affluent ones said﴾: "They are their leaders and their nobles."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿And thus We did not send before you any warner into a town but its affluent ones said﴾: "Their leaders and their heads in polytheism."

* * *

As for His saying, ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion (ummah)﴾:

He says: They said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a creed and a religion," ﴿and indeed we are following in their footsteps﴾, meaning: and indeed we are following their path and their way, acting as they acted, and worshipping what they used to worship. Thus His exalted praise says to Muhammad ﷺ: The polytheists of your people have only followed the path of those before them, their brethren among the people of polytheism in Allah, in their response to you with what they responded with, and their rejection of what they rejected from your counsel, and their argument with what they argued to justify their standing upon their false religion.

And with something similar to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿and indeed we are following in their footsteps﴾: "By their deeds."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and indeed we are following in their footsteps﴾: "So they followed them in that."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verses 24–25:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Even if I brought you better guidance than that which you found your fathers following?" They said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent."﴾ (24)

His Exalted mention says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists from your people, who say, "We found our fathers following a community, and we are guided by their footsteps": ﴿Even if I brought you, O people, from your Lord,﴾ ﴿better guidance﴾ to the path of truth, and more indicative for you of the way of right guidance, ﴿than that which you found your fathers upon﴾ of religion and creed. ﴿They said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent."﴾ He says: so he said that to them, and they answered him by saying to him what those before them among the nations that denied their messengers said to their prophets: "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, O people," meaning: deniers and rejecters.

The readers of the metropolitan cities recited this verse as "Qul awa law ji'tukum" with the letter ta (tā'), except Abu Ja'far. It is mentioned from the reader Abu Ja'far that he recited it as "Qul awa law jinakum" with the letter nun and alif.

Our view is that the recitation is what the readers of the metropolitan cities hold, because the consensus of the proof (ijma' al-hujja) rests upon it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So We took retribution from them. So observe how was the end of the deniers.﴾ (25)

His Exalted mention says: So We took retribution from these people who denied their messengers, among the disbelieving nations who disbelieved in their Lord, by inflicting punishment upon them. So observe, O Muhammad, how the outcome of their affair was, when they denied the signs of God. By His saying ﴿the end of the deniers﴾ He means the final outcome of those who denied the messengers of God, where it ended: Did We not destroy them and make them a lesson for others?

As:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verses 24–25:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Even if I brought you better guidance than that which you found your fathers following?" They said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent."﴾ (24)

His Exalted mention says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists from your people, who say, "We found our fathers following a community, and we are guided by their footsteps": ﴿Even if I brought you, O people, from your Lord,﴾ ﴿better guidance﴾ to the path of truth, and more indicative for you of the way of right guidance, ﴿than that which you found your fathers upon﴾ of religion and creed. ﴿They said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent."﴾ He says: so he said that to them, and they answered him by saying to him what those before them among the nations that denied their messengers said to their prophets: "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, O people," meaning: deniers and rejecters.

The readers of the metropolitan cities recited this verse as "Qul awa law ji'tukum" with the letter ta (tā'), except Abu Ja'far. It is mentioned from the reader Abu Ja'far that he recited it as "Qul awa law jinakum" with the letter nun and alif.

Our view is that the recitation is what the readers of the metropolitan cities hold, because the consensus of the proof (ijma' al-hujja) rests upon it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So We took retribution from them. So observe how was the end of the deniers.﴾ (25)

His Exalted mention says: So We took retribution from these people who denied their messengers, among the disbelieving nations who disbelieved in their Lord, by inflicting punishment upon them. So observe, O Muhammad, how the outcome of their affair was, when they denied the signs of God. By His saying ﴿the end of the deniers﴾ He means the final outcome of those who denied the messengers of God, where it ended: Did We not destroy them and make them a lesson for others?

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So We took retribution from them. So observe how was the end of the deniers.﴾ He said: Evil, by God; He seized them with sinking and drowning, then destroyed them and made them enter the Fire.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verses 26–28:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free from what you worship, (26) except He who created me, for He will guide me." (27) And He made it a word remaining among his descendants that they might return.﴾ (28)

Exalted is He, says: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father and his people﴾, those who used to worship what the polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, worship, ﴿"Indeed, I am free from what you worship"﴾ besides Allah. So they denied him, and We took vengeance upon them, as We took vengeance upon those before them, of the nations that denied their messengers. It has also been said: ﴿"Indeed, I am free from what you worship"﴾, where "barā'" (free from), which is a verbal noun (masdar), is placed in the position of a descriptive adjective (na't). The Arabs do not make "barā'" dual, plural, or feminine. So they say: "We are barā' (free from) and khalā' (empty of)," because of what I mentioned, that it is a masdar. But when they say: "He is bari' (free) from you," they make it dual, plural and feminine, saying: "They two are bari'ān (free) from you," and "They are bari'ūn (free) from you." It is also reported that in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "Innanī bari'" with the letter yā'. And the plural of bari' may be barā' and abrā'.

﴿Except He who created me﴾: he says, "I am free from whatever you worship, except from He who created me," meaning He who brought me into being. ﴿For He will guide me﴾: he says, "For He will set me upright upon the true religion, and grant me success in following the path of rectitude."

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father and his people﴾ ... the verse, he said: "He was deceiving them. They used to say: 'Allah is our Lord,' ﴿And if you asked them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they would surely say, 'Allah'﴾, so he did not disavow his Lord."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿"Indeed, I am free from what you worship"﴾, he said: "Indeed, I am free from what you worship, ﴿except He who created me﴾."

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿except He who created me﴾, he said: "He created me."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He made it a word remaining among his descendants﴾

Exalted is He, says: He made His saying, ﴿"Indeed, I am free from what you worship, except He who created me"﴾, which is the statement "There is no god but Allah," a word remaining among his descendants, who are his offspring. So there has always been among his descendants someone who says it after him.

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of the word which the Friend of the Most Merciful made remain among his descendants. Some of them said: it is in accordance with what we have said about it.

Those who said so:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And He made it a word remaining among his descendants﴾, he said: "There is no god but Allah."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And He made it a word remaining﴾, he said: "The testimony that there is no god but Allah, and monotheism, has never ceased among his descendants; there has always been someone among them who says it after him."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And He made it a word remaining among his descendants﴾, he said: "Monotheism and sincerity; and there never ceases to be among his descendants someone who affirms the oneness of Allah and worships Him."

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿among his descendants﴾, he said: "There is no god but Allah."

Others said: the word which Allah made among his descendants is the name of Islam.

Those who said so:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And He made it a word remaining among his descendants﴾, he recited ﴿When his Lord said to him, "Submit," he said, "I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds"﴾, and said: "He made this remain among his descendants, [namely] Islam." He also recited ﴿He named you Muslims before [in former scriptures]﴾, and recited ﴿and make us Muslims [in submission] to You﴾.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about the meaning of "descendants" ('aqib).

Those who said so:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿among his descendants﴾, he said: "His offspring."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And He made it a word remaining among his descendants﴾, he said: "That is, among those who succeed him."

Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿among his descendants﴾, he said: "Among the descendants of Abraham, the family of Muhammad ﷺ."

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, that he used to say: "The 'aqib is the offspring, and the offspring's offspring."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿among his descendants﴾: "His 'aqib is his progeny."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿that they might return﴾

He says: that they might return to obedience to their Lord, turn back to His worship, and repent from their disbelief and sins.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿that they might return﴾: "i.e., that they might repent, or be reminded."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verses 31–32:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from the two cities?" Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the worldly life, and raised some of them above others in degrees, so that some of them may take others in service. Actually, following the instruction to translate the passage exactly as given, here is the faithful translation of the text provided:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And were it not that mankind would become one community, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver ceilings for their houses and stairways upon which they could ascend﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be a community﴾: one single group.

Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the matter whose collective occurrence was not to be trusted, had He done what He said, and what prevented Him from doing it on account of it. Some of them said: That is their gathering upon disbelief. He said: The meaning of the speech is: And were it not that mankind would be one community upon disbelief, so that all of them would become disbelievers, ﴿We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver ceilings for their houses﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community﴾, he said: God, glorified is He, says: Were it not that I would make all people disbelievers, I would have made for the disbelievers silver ceilings for their houses.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Hawdhah ibn Khalifah narrated to us, he said: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community﴾, he said: Were it not that all people would be disbelievers, inclining towards the world, Allah, blessed and exalted is He, would have done what He said. Then he said: By God, the world has inclined most of its people, and He did not do that, so how much more if He had done it.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community﴾: i.e., all of them disbelievers.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community﴾, he said: Were it not that the people would be disbelievers.

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community﴾, he said: disbelievers upon one religion.

Others said: Their gathering upon seeking the world and abandoning seeking the Hereafter. He said: The meaning of the speech is: And were it not that mankind would be one community upon seeking the world and forsaking the Hereafter.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Yunus narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿And were it not that mankind would be one community﴾, he said: Were it not that people would prefer their worldly life over their religion, We would have made this for the people of disbelief.

* *

And His saying: ﴿We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful silver ceilings for their houses﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful in this world ceilings, meaning the upper parts of their houses, which are the roofs, of silver.

As:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿silver ceilings for their houses﴾: the ceiling is the upper part of the houses.

The grammarians differed concerning the repetition of the lam in His saying ﴿for those who disbelieve﴾ and in His saying ﴿for their houses﴾. Some grammarians of Basra claimed that it was introduced into "houses" as a substitution (badal). Some grammarians of Kufa said: If you wish, you may take it as repeated in ﴿for their houses﴾, as in ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it﴾; and if you wish, you may make the two lams different, as if the second has the meaning of ʿala (upon), as if He said: We made for them upon their houses ceilings. He said: The Arabs say to a man in his presence: I made for you for your people the gifts, meaning: I made it for them on your account.

The reciters differed in reading His saying "suqufan" (ceilings). The majority of the reciters of Mecca, some of the Medinans, and the majority of the Basrans read ﴿saqfan﴾ with a fatha on the sin and a sukun on the qaf, considering it in light of His saying: ﴿the roof fell upon them from above them﴾, and directing it to the fact that it is one word whose meaning is plural. Some reciters of Medina and the majority of the reciters of Kufa read ﴿suqufan﴾ with a damma on the sin and the qaf, and they directed it to its being the plural of saqifah or suquf. If it is directed to its being the plural of suquf, it would be a plural of a plural, because suquf is the plural of saqf, and then suquf is pluralized as saqf; this is analogous to the reading of one who read "fa-ruhunun maqbudah" with a damma on the ra and the ha, which is a plural, its singular being rihan and rihun, and the singular of rihun and rihan is rahn.

Likewise the reading of one who read "kulu min thumurihi" with a damma on the tha and the mim, and analogous to the saying of the rajiz:

Until, when the throats of the gullets became wet [[The verse is cited in Lisan al-Arab (root h-l-q) without attribution, and perhaps it is by Ru'bah. Al-Halq: the passage of food and drink in the gullet; the small plural is ahlaq, and the large plural is hulud and hulq. And in the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' (folio 295) he said at His saying, the Exalted: "for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful, for their houses ceilings": "suqufan" was read by ʿAsim and al-Aʿmash as "saqfan" (i.e., with a fatha on the sin and a sukun on the qaf). If you wish, make its singular "saqifah," and if you wish, make it "suqufan," which is a plural of a plural, as the poet said: * until, when the throats of the gullets became wet *

He inclined to the nearest step on the edge [of the valley] *

And similar is the reading of one who read "kulu min thamarihi" (with a damma on the tha and the mim), which is a plural whose singular is thimar; and like the reading of one who read "fa-rihanun maqbudah" whose singular is "rihan" and "rihun." End quote.

Some of them claimed that suqf with a damma on the sin and the qaf is the plural of saqf, and ruhun with a damma on the ra and the ha is the plural of rahn, but they overlooked the correct aspect of this, because in the speech of the Arabs there is no noun on the pattern fa'l with a fatha on the first letter and a sukun on the middle letter pluralized as fu'ul, so that suqf and ruhun could be made analogous to it.

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is that they are two readings close in meaning, both known in the readings of the regions, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

And His saying: ﴿and stairways upon which they could ascend﴾

He says: and ladders and steps upon which they ascend, so that they would appear upon the ceilings. The ma'arij are the steps themselves, as the poet al-Muthanna ibn Jandal said:

O Lord, Lord of the house of the ma'arij [[The verse is attributed by the author to al-Muthanna ibn Jandal. Abu Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 220b) attributed it to Jandal ibn al-Muthanna, which is correct; he is Jandal ibn al-Muthanna al-Tuhawi, as in Simt al-Lali (702). He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We made for their houses doors of silver, and couches of silver.

As:

* Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "and couches": he said, "couches of silver."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And for their houses, doors and couches on which they recline﴾, he said: "The doors are of silver, and the couches of silver, on which they recline." He means: they recline on the couches.

* * *

And His words: ﴿And ornaments of gold﴾

He says: And We would have made for them, in addition to that, ornaments, which is gold.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And ornaments of gold﴾: it is gold.

* Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And ornaments of gold﴾, he said: "Gold." And al-Hasan said: "A house of zukhruf," he said: "gold."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And ornaments of gold﴾: "Zukhruf is gold." He said: "By Allah, they used to dislike garments of fame." And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "Beware of red, for it is among the most beloved adornments to Satan."

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And ornaments of gold﴾: "Gold."

* Ahmad [[It appears that this is repeated.]] narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And ornaments of gold﴾: "Gold."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And ornaments of gold﴾: "He would have given this to the people of disbelief, meaning for their houses a roof of silver and what is mentioned with it.
