Ibn al-Muthannā related to us, saying: Ibn Abī ʿAdī related to us, from Shuʿbah, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, similarly.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, saying: ʿĪsā related to us; and al-Ḥārith related to me, saying: al-Ḥasan related to us, saying: Warqāʾ related to us, all of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿When your people turn away from it in dismay﴾ He said: they cry out.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: ﴿When your people turn away from it in dismay﴾: that is, they become distressed and cry out.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read it ﴿yaṣuddūna﴾: that is, they cry out; and ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him) read ﴿yaṣuddūna﴾.

I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd related to us, who said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, regarding His saying: ﴿When your people turn away from it in dismay﴾: they cry out.

Muhammad related to us, saying: Aḥmad related to us, saying: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: ﴿When your people turn away from it in dismay﴾ He said: they cry out.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verses 58–60:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And they say: Are our gods better, or is he? They have not cited it to you except for disputation. Nay, they are a contentious people.﴾ (58) ﴿He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel.﴾ (59) ﴿And if We willed, We would have made among you angels to succeed you on the earth.﴾ (60)

His, may He be remembered and exalted, saying: The polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, said: Are our gods, which we worship, better? Or is Muhammad better, so that we worship Muhammad and abandon our gods?

It is mentioned that this is in the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Are our gods better, or is this one?"

The narration with this: Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, that in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "And they said: Are our gods better, or is this one?" meaning Muhammad (ﷺ).

Others said: Rather, by this is meant: Are our gods better, or is Jesus?

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿And they say: Are our gods better, or is he? They have not cited it to you except for disputation. Nay, they are a contentious people.﴾ He said: They disputed with him, saying: He claims that everyone who has been worshipped besides Allah is in the Fire; we are content that our gods be with Jesus, Uzayr and the angels, who have been worshipped besides Allah. He said: Then Allah revealed the exoneration of Jesus.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Are our gods better?﴾ He said: These worshipped Jesus, and we worship the angels.

* *

As for His words: ﴿They have not cited it to you except for disputation. Nay, they are a contentious people.﴾

... up to ﴿who will succeed on the earth.﴾ His, may He be remembered and exalted, words: ﴿They have not cited it to you except for disputation﴾ mean: they have not coined this parable for you, O Muhammad, nor said this statement to you, except as disputation and contention with which they contest you. ﴿Nay, they are a contentious people﴾ — He, may His praise be great, says: Your people, O Muhammad, these polytheists, in their argument with you, do not seek the truth by what they argue with you; ﴿nay, they are a contentious people﴾ who seek contention through falsehood.

It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "No people have strayed from the truth except that they were given to disputation."

The narration of that: Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ya'la related to us, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn Dinar related to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No people have strayed after guidance they were upon except that they were given to disputation," and he recited: ﴿They have not cited it to you except for disputation﴾ ... the verse.

Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Kindi and Abu Kurayb related to me, both saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr related to us, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn Dinar related to us, from Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to the people while they were disputing about the Qur'an, and he became exceedingly angry, as if vinegar had been poured on his face, and then he (ﷺ) said: "Do not strike the Book of Allah one part against another, for no people have ever strayed except that they were given to disputation," then he recited: ﴿They have not cited it to you except for disputation. Nay, they are a contentious people.﴾

* *

As for His words: ﴿He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour﴾

His, may He be remembered and exalted, saying: Jesus is only a servant of Our servants, upon whom We bestowed favour by guidance and faith, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel — that is, We made him a sign for the Children of Israel and a proof for Us against them, by sending him to them calling to Us; and he is not, as the Christians say, the son of Allah, exalted is Allah above that.

Those of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour﴾ — by this is meant Jesus son of Mary; apart from that, Jesus son of Mary, if he was only a servant upon whom Allah bestowed favour.

And they said the like of what we have said also regarding His words: ﴿And We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾.

Those who said that:

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿an example for the Children of Israel﴾ — I think he said: a sign for the Children of Israel.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾ — that is, a sign.

* *

His words: ﴿And if We willed, We would have made among you angels to succeed you on the earth﴾

His, may He be remembered and exalted, saying: And if We willed, O assembly of the children of Adam, We would have destroyed you and annihilated all of you, and placed in your stead on the earth angels who would succeed you there, worshipping Me. This is like His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿If He wills, He will remove you, O people, and bring others; and Allah is ever capable of that﴾ and as He said: ﴿If He wills, He will remove you and make succeed after you whom He wills.﴾

The interpreters have said the like of what we have said about this, except that some of them said: its meaning is: some of them succeed others.

Those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And if We willed, We would have made among you angels to succeed you on the earth﴾, he said: some of them succeed others.

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿We would have made among you angels on the earth who would succeed﴾, he said: they would populate the earth in your stead.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿angels on the earth who would succeed﴾, he said: some of them succeed others, in place of the children of Adam.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And if We willed, We would have made among you angels to succeed you on the earth﴾ — if Allah willed, He would have placed angels on the earth succeeding one another.

Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And if We willed, We would have made among you angels to succeed you on the earth﴾, he said: successors from among you.

His words: ﴿And if We willed, We would have made among you angels to succeed you on the earth﴾

His, may He be remembered and exalted, saying: And if We willed, O assembly of the children of Adam, We would have destroyed you and annihilated all of you, and placed in your stead on the earth angels who would succeed you there, worshipping Me. This is like His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿If He wills, He will remove you, O people, and bring others; and Allah is ever capable of that﴾ and as He said: ﴿If He wills, He will remove you and make succeed after you whom He wills.﴾

The interpreters have said the like of what we have said about this, except that some of them said: its meaning is: some of them succeed others.

Those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And if We willed, We would have made among you angels to succeed you on the earth﴾, he said: some of them succeed others.

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿We would have made among you angels on the earth who would succeed﴾, he said: they would populate the earth in your stead.

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿angels on the earth who would succeed﴾, he said: some of them succeed others, in place of the children of Adam.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And if We willed, We would have made among you angels to succeed you on the earth﴾ — if Allah willed, He would have placed angels on the earth succeeding one another.

Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And if We willed, We would have made among you angels to succeed you on the earth﴾, he said: successors from among you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verses 58–60:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And they say: Are our gods better, or is he? They have not cited it to you except for disputation. Nay, they are a contentious people.﴾ (58) ﴿He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel.﴾ (59) ﴿And if We willed, We would have made among you angels to succeed you on the earth.﴾ (60)

His, may He be remembered and exalted, saying: The polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, said: Are our gods, which we worship, better? Or is Muhammad better, so that we worship Muhammad and abandon our gods?

It is mentioned that this is in the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Are our gods better, or is this one?"

The narration with this: Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, that in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "And they said: Are our gods better, or is this one?" meaning Muhammad (ﷺ).

Others said: Rather, by this is meant: Are our gods better, or is Jesus?

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿And they say: Are our gods better, or is he? They have not cited it to you except for disputation. Nay, they are a contentious people.﴾ He said: They disputed with him, saying: He claims that everyone who has been worshipped besides Allah is in the Fire; we are content that our gods be with Jesus, Uzayr and the angels, who have been worshipped besides Allah. He said: Then Allah revealed the exoneration of Jesus.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Are our gods better?﴾ He said: These worshipped Jesus, and we worship the angels.

* *

As for His words: ﴿They have not cited it to you except for disputation. Nay, they are a contentious people.﴾

... up to ﴿who will succeed on the earth.﴾ His, may He be remembered and exalted, words: ﴿They have not cited it to you except for disputation﴾ mean: they have not coined this parable for you, O Muhammad, nor said this statement to you, except as disputation and contention with which they contest you. ﴿Nay, they are a contentious people﴾ — He, may His praise be great, says: Your people, O Muhammad, these polytheists, in their argument with you, do not seek the truth by what they argue with you; ﴿nay, they are a contentious people﴾ who seek contention through falsehood.

It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "No people have strayed from the truth except that they were given to disputation."

The narration of that: Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ya'la related to us, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn Dinar related to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No people have strayed after guidance they were upon except that they were given to disputation," and he recited: ﴿They have not cited it to you except for disputation﴾ ... the verse.

Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Kindi and Abu Kurayb related to me, both saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr related to us, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn Dinar related to us, from Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to the people while they were disputing about the Qur'an, and he became exceedingly angry, as if vinegar had been poured on his face, and then he (ﷺ) said: "Do not strike the Book of Allah one part against another, for no people have ever strayed except that they were given to disputation," then he recited: ﴿They have not cited it to you except for disputation. Nay, they are a contentious people.﴾

* *

As for His words: ﴿He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour﴾

His, may He be remembered and exalted, saying: Jesus is only a servant of Our servants, upon whom We bestowed favour by guidance and faith, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel — that is, We made him a sign for the Children of Israel and a proof for Us against them, by sending him to them calling to Us; and he is not, as the Christians say, the son of Allah, exalted is Allah above that.

Those of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour﴾ — by this is meant Jesus son of Mary; apart from that, Jesus son of Mary, if he was only a servant upon whom Allah bestowed favour.

And they said the like of what we have said also regarding His words: ﴿And We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾.

Those who said that:

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿an example for the Children of Israel﴾ — I think he said: a sign for the Children of Israel.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾ — that is, a sign.

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 61–62:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, it is a sign of the Hour, so do not doubt it, and follow Me. This is a straight path.﴾ (61) ﴿And let not Satan avert you, for he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ (62)

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the pronoun in His saying ﴿wa-innahu﴾ (and indeed it), what it refers to, and who mentioned what it is. Some of them said: it refers to Jesus, and it returns to him. They said: the meaning of the statement is: "And indeed Jesus, his appearance is a knowledge by which the coming of the Hour is known, because his appearance is one of its portents, and his descent to the earth is evidence of the passing away of this world and the approach of the Hereafter."

Mention of those who said that:

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAsim, from Abu Razin, from Yahya, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿And indeed, it is a knowledge of the Hour﴾, he said: "The emergence of Jesus son of Mary."

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from ʿAsim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn ʿAbbas, with the like of it, except that he said: "The descent of Jesus son of Mary."

• Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to me, he said: Ghalib ibn Qa'id narrated to us, he said: Qays narrated to us, from ʿAsim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he used to recite "wa-innahu la-ʿalamun lil-sāʿah" and said: "The descent of Jesus son of Mary."

• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn ʿAtiyyah narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from Jabir, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas used to say: "I do not know whether people know the interpretation of this verse, or did not perceive it?" "And indeed, it is a knowledge of the Hour," he said: "The descent of Jesus son of Mary."

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "And indeed, it is a knowledge of the Hour," he said: "The descent of Jesus son of Mary."

• Yaʿqub narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: Husayn informed us, from Abu Malik and ʿAwf, from al-Hasan, that they both said concerning His saying ﴿And indeed, it is a knowledge of the Hour﴾: "The descent of Jesus son of Mary." And one of them recited it as "wa-innahu la-ʿalamun lil-sāʿah."

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿And indeed, it is a knowledge of the Hour﴾: "It is a sign of the Hour: the emergence of Jesus son of Mary before the Day of Resurrection."

• Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, "wa-innahu la-ʿalamun lil-sāʿah," he said: "The descent of Jesus son of Mary is a knowledge of the Hour: the Resurrection."

• Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His saying "wa-innahu la-ʿalamun lil-sāʿah," he said: "The descent of Jesus son of Mary is a knowledge of the Hour."

• Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿And indeed, it is a knowledge of the Hour﴾, he said: "The emergence of Jesus son of Mary before the Day of Resurrection."

• It was related to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿And indeed, it is a knowledge of the Hour﴾: "He means the emergence of Jesus son of Mary and his descent from heaven before the Day of Resurrection."

• Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And indeed, it is a knowledge of the Hour﴾: "The descent of Jesus son of Mary is a knowledge of the Hour when he descends."

Others said: the pronoun in His saying ﴿wa-innahu﴾ refers to the Qur'an, and they said: the meaning of the statement is: "And indeed this Qur'an is a knowledge of the Hour, informing you of its establishment and telling you about it and its terrors."

Mention of those who said that:

• Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan used to say: "wa-innahu la-ʿalamun lil-sāʿah" is this Qur'an.

• Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: some people used to say: "The Qur'an is a knowledge of the Hour." The readers of the regions agreed on reading His saying ﴿wa-innahu la-ʿilmun lil-sāʿah﴾ with a kasrah on the ʿayn of ʿilm. And it is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, what I mentioned from him, that it is read with a fatha, as well as from Qatadah and al-Dahhak.

The correct reading in this matter is the kasrah on the ʿayn, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

It has been mentioned that in the reading of Ubayy it is "wa-innahu la-dhikrun lis-sāʿah" (and indeed it is a reminder of the Hour), and this confirms the reading of those who read with a kasrah on the ʿayn in His saying ﴿la-ʿilmun﴾.

His saying ﴿fa-lā tamtarunna bihā﴾

He says: so do not doubt in it and in its coming, O people.

As:

• Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿So do not doubt in it﴾, he said: "Do not doubt it."

* *

His saying ﴿wa-ittabiʿūn﴾

His exalted remembrance says: and obey Me, act upon what I have commanded you, and desist from what I have forbidden you. ﴿This is a straight path﴾: your following of me, O people, in My command and My prohibition is a straight path. He says: a road in which there is no crookedness, rather it is upright.

* *

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said: "I have certainly come to you with wisdom, and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ, so fear Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path."﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "When Jesus came to the Children of Israel with clear proofs," meaning with manifest evidences. It has also been said that by "clear proofs" is meant the Gospel (al-Injil).

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And when Jesus came with clear proofs﴾: that is, with the Gospel.

* *

As for His words: ﴿He said: "I have certainly come to you with wisdom"﴾

It has been said that by "wisdom" in this place is meant prophethood.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿I have certainly come to you with wisdom﴾: he said, "Prophethood."

I have already explained the meaning of wisdom earlier in this book of ours, with its evidences, and mentioned the differing views of those who differed concerning its interpretation, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ﴾

He says: "And I will make clear to you, O assembly of the Children of Israel, some of what you differ about regarding the rulings of the Torah."

As narrated:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ﴾: he said, "From the alteration of the Torah."

It has also been said that "some" (ba'd) in this place carries the meaning of "all" (kull), and they took this as analogous to the verse of Labid:

*Tarrak amkinatin idha lam arduha... aw ya'taliq ba'da al-nufusi hamamuha*

[Labid's verse is cited by Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (fol. 221) when explaining the verse "to make clear to you some of that about which you differ," where he said: "al-ba'd here means kull (all)," and recited Labid's verse. Al-Zawzani, in his commentary on the Seven Mu'allaqat (p. 116), explains that the poet means: I abandon places I find distasteful, unless death restrains me, and it does not allow me to depart. By "some of the souls" he meant his own soul. This is the most correct and best of the opinions. Whoever takes "some of the souls" to mean "all the souls" has erred, because "some" does not imply generality and comprehensiveness. The precise meaning is: I do not stay in places I find repugnant, I leave them and turn away, unless I die. Al-Tibrizi, in his commentary on the Ten Odes (p. 160), says: "He means: I leave places when I see in them what is disliked, unless death overtakes me, and by 'souls' he means himself; yaʿtaliq means 'is held back'; al-hamam means death, and it is also said [it means] fate. His saying 'aw ya'taliq' is in the jussive, coordinated with his saying 'idha lam arduha.'" End of quotation.]

Some have said: "Death does not hold back some souls; rather the meaning is: 'or death holds back souls.'" But this speaker's view has no great meaning, because Jesus only said to them, "and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ," since there was much disagreement among them concerning the affairs of their religion and their worldly life. So he told them: "I will make clear to you some of that, namely the matters of your religion, apart from what you differ about in your worldly affairs." Therefore he restricted what he informed them he would make clear. Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said: "I have certainly come to you with wisdom, and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ, so fear Allah and obey me. He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "When Jesus came to the Children of Israel with clear proofs," meaning with manifest evidences. It has also been said that by "clear proofs" is meant the Gospel (al-Injil).

Mention of those who said this:

* *

He says: "And I will make clear to you, O assembly of the Children of Israel, some of what you differ about regarding the rulings of the Torah."

As narrated:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ﴾: he said, "From the alteration of the Torah."

It has also been said that "some" (ba'd) in this place carries the meaning of "all" (kull), and they took this as analogous to the verse of Labid:

*Tarrak amkinatin idha lam arduha... aw ya'taliq ba'da al-nufusi hamamuha*

[Labid's verse is cited by Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an (fol. 221) when explaining the verse "to make clear to you some of that about which you differ," where he said: "al-ba'd here means kull (all)," and recited Labid's verse. By "some of the souls" he meant his own soul. This is the most correct and best of the opinions. Whoever takes "some of the souls" to mean "all the souls" has erred, because "some" does not imply generality and comprehensiveness. The precise meaning is: I do not stay in places I find repugnant, I leave them and turn away, unless I die. Al-Tibrizi, in his commentary on the Ten Odes (p. 160), says: "He means: I leave places when I see in them what is disliked, unless death overtakes me, and by 'souls' he means himself; yaʿtaliq means 'is held back'; al-hamam means death, and it is also said [it means] fate. His saying 'aw ya'taliq' is in the jussive, coordinated with his saying 'idha lam arduha.'" End of quotation.]

Some have said: "Death does not hold back some souls; rather the meaning is: 'or death holds back souls.'" But this speaker's view has no great meaning, because Jesus only said to them, "and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ," since there was much disagreement among them concerning the affairs of their religion and their worldly life. So he told them: "I will make clear to you some of that, namely the matters of your religion, apart from what you differ about in your worldly affairs." Therefore he restricted what he informed them he would make clear. **The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿So the factions differed among themselves. Woe, then, to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful day.﴾ (43:65) ﴿Do they await anything but the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly while they perceive not?﴾ (43:66)**

The scholars of tafsir (exegesis) differed about who is meant by "the factions" that Allah mentions in this verse. Some of them said: it refers to the group that disputed about the affair of Jesus and differed concerning him.

Those who said this:

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿So the factions differed among themselves﴾, he said: "They are the four whom the Children of Israel sent out, saying things about Jesus."

Others said: rather, they are the Jews and the Christians.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿So the factions differed among themselves﴾, he said: "The Jews and the Christians."

The correct view on this matter is to say: the meaning is: the sects that differed concerning Jesus son of Mary differed from among those whom Jesus called to what he called them to, namely the fear of Allah and acting in obedience to Him. They are the Jews and the Christians, and those among the Christians who differed concerning him, because all of them were factions [[As in the original. Perhaps the correct reading is "mutabasilin" with the tāʾ before the bāʾ. In Lisan al-ʿArab: tabasala al-rajul: he frowned from anger or from bravery. As for ibtasala al-rajul with the bāʾ first, it means: he took a wage for his [spiritual] protection.]] of divergent desires, while he (Jesus) had made clear to them the matter of himself, and his words to them: ﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾

* *

As for His words: ﴿So woe to those who did wrong from the punishment of a painful day﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: So there is (for them) the valley flowing with pus and matter in Hell, for those who disbelieved in Allah, who spoke about Jesus son of Mary contrary to how Jesus described himself in this verse. ﴿From the punishment of a painful day﴾: that is, from the punishment of a day that is painful. The day is described as painful because the punishment in it causes them pain, and that day is the Day of Resurrection.

As related:

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿from the punishment of a painful day﴾, he said: "From the punishment of the Day of Resurrection."

* *

As for His words: ﴿Do they await anything but the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly﴾

He says: Do these factions who differed concerning Jesus son of Mary, who utter falsehood about him, await anything but the Hour in which the Resurrection will occur suddenly? ﴿While they perceive not﴾: that is, while they do not know of its coming.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 67–68:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the God-fearing﴾ [43:67] ﴿O My servants, no fear shall be upon you this Day, nor shall you grieve﴾ [43:68].

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Those who befriended one another in disobedience to God in the world will be on the Day of Resurrection enemies to one another; some of them will disown others, except those who had befriended one another in the world out of fear of God.

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the God-fearing﴾: every friendship in the world founded on disobedience to God will be enmity.

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding his saying: ﴿Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the God-fearing﴾: every friendship that is (rooted in disobedience) will be enmity, except the friendship of the God-fearing.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ishaq, that Ali (may God be pleased with him) said: Two believing friends and two disbelieving friends. When one of the believing friends dies, he says: "O Lord, so-and-so used to command me to obey You and Your Messenger, command me to do good, forbid me from evil, and inform me that I will meet You. O Lord, do not let him go astray after me, guide him as You guided me, and honour him as You honoured me." When his believing friend dies, He gathers the two of them and says: "Let each of you praise his companion." So one of them says: "O Lord, he used to command me to obey You and Your Messenger, command me to do good, forbid me from evil, and inform me that I will meet You." He says: "Excellent friend, excellent brother, excellent companion." He said: And when one of the two disbelievers dies, he says: "O Lord, so-and-so used to forbid me from obeying You and Your Messenger, command me to do evil, forbid me from good, and inform me that I will not meet You." He says: "Wretched brother, wretched friend, wretched companion."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿O My servants, no fear shall be upon you this Day, nor shall you grieve﴾

In this statement there is an omission, which is dispensed with by the indication of what has been mentioned. The meaning of the statement is: "Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the God-fearing; for they will be told: 'O My servants, no fear shall be upon you this Day from My punishment, for I have granted you security from it through My pleasure with you, nor shall you grieve over leaving the world, for what you have come to is better for you than what you have left behind in it.'"

It is mentioned that people will be called with this call on the Day of Resurrection, so that one who is not of its people will hope for it until he hears His saying: ﴿Those who believed in Our signs and were Muslims﴾ [43:69], and at that point he despairs of it.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, who said: I heard that when people are resurrected, none of them will be without terror, and a herald will call out: "O servants of God, no fear shall be upon you this Day, nor shall you grieve." All the people will hope for it, and then ﴿Those who believed in Our signs and were Muslims﴾ will follow it. He said: So the people, other than the Muslims, will despair of it.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those who believed in Our signs and were Muslims (submitters). Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, delighted.﴾

And His saying: ﴿Those who believed in Our signs﴾

And His saying: ﴿Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, delighted﴾

He, may His majesty be praised, says: Enter Paradise, you, O believers, and your spouses, envied for the honour of Allah, rejoicing in what your Lord has given you today.

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, the Exalted: ﴿They will be served with dishes of gold, and goblets; and in it is whatever the souls desire and whatever delights the eyes, and you will abide therein eternally﴾ (43:71)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: They will be served, these who believed in His signs in the world, when they enter Paradise in the Hereafter, with dishes of gold. Ṣiḥāf is the plural of the many of ṣaḥfah, and the ṣaḥfah is a large bowl (qaṣʿah).

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

- Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: Aḥmad narrated to us, he said: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, regarding ﴿They will be served with dishes of gold﴾, he said: "The qiṣāʿ (large bowls)."

- Abū Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Yamān narrated to us, from Ashʿath ibn Isḥāq, from Jaʿfar, from Shuʿbah, he said: "Indeed, the lowest in rank among the people of Paradise is one who has a palace in which there are seventy thousand servants, in the hand of each servant a dish, apart from what is in the hand of its owner. If its door were opened, it would accommodate the people of the world, and it would be wide enough for them."

- Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, he said: Yaʿqūb al-Qummī narrated to us, Jaʿfar, from Saʿīd, he said: "Indeed, the lowest in rank among the people of Paradise is one who has seventy thousand servants, with each servant a dish of gold. If all the people of the earth were to descend upon him, it would be wide enough for them, and he would not seek help against them with anything from elsewhere. And that is in the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿For them is whatever they wish therein, and with Us is more﴾ [50:35]. And for them ﴿and in it is whatever the souls desire and whatever delights the eyes﴾."

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Abū Ayyūb al-Azdī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, he said: "No one among the people of Paradise is without a thousand boys attending him, each boy performing a task different from that of his companion."

* *

And His words: ﴿and goblets﴾

It is the plural of kūb, and the kūb is a jug with a rounded head that has no handle (udhn) and no spout (khurṭūm). It is to this that al-Aʿshā referred in his saying:

ṣarīfiyyatun ṭayyibun ṭaʿmuhā ... lahā zabadun bayna kūbin wa dann [[The verse is by Aʿshā ibn Qays of Banū Thaʿlabah (his Dīwān, Cairo edition, p. 17). Ṣarīfiyyah is attributed to Ṣarīfūn, a place in Iraq famous for the quality of its wine. It is also said to be attributed to al-ṣarīf, which is milk at the moment it is milked; it was called ṣarīfiyyah because it was taken from the jar at the very moment it was brought out, as if it were taken before being mixed. Zabad: the foam that rises on it when it is transferred from the jar to the goblet, from the bubbles. Kūb: a jug that has no handle. Or it is the jug with a rounded head that has no spout.]]

The people of ta'wil said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

- Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: Aḥmad narrated to us, he said: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, regarding ﴿and goblets﴾, he said: "The goblets are those that have no spouts."

The meaning of the speech is: They will be served therein with food in dishes of gold, and with drink in goblets of gold. So the mention of the dishes and goblets is sufficient in place of mentioning the food and drink that will be in them, because the hearers know its meaning.

﴿And in it is whatever the souls desire and whatever delights the eyes﴾ He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: For you in Paradise is whatever your souls desire, O believers, and whatever delights your eyes. ﴿And you will abide therein eternally﴾ means: You will remain therein forever, never leaving it.

As follows:

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad, from Ibn Sābiṭ, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I love horses; is there horses in Paradise?" He said: "If Allah admits you into Paradise, if He wills, you will not desire to ride a horse of red ruby which flies with you to whichever part of Paradise you wish, except that it will do so." A Bedouin then said: "O Messenger of Allah, I love camels; is there camels in Paradise?" He said: "O Bedouin, if Allah admits you into Paradise, if Allah wills, there will be in it whatever your soul desires and whatever delights your eyes" (ﷺ).

- al-Ḥasan ibn ʿArafah narrated to us, he said: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Abbār narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd al-Anṣārī, from Abū Ẓabyah al-Salafī, he said: "Indeed, the company of people of Paradise, a cloud will shade them, and it will say: 'What shall I rain upon you?' So no one from the group calls for anything except that it rains it upon them, until the speaker among them says: 'Rain upon us maidens with swelling breasts, of equal age.'"

- Ibn ʿArafah narrated to us, he said: Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī al-Walīd, he said: "It was said to Mujāhid: Is there music in Paradise? He said: 'Indeed, in it there is a tree called al-ʿĪṣ, which has a sound that the listeners have never heard the likes of.'"

- Mūsā ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to me, he said: Zayd ibn Ḥabbāb narrated to us, he said: Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ informed us, he said: Sulaymān ibn ʿĀmir narrated to me, he said: I heard Abū Umāmah say: "Indeed, a man of the people of Paradise desires a bird and it is flying, and it falls split and roasted into his palm, so he eats from it until his soul is satisfied; then it flies off. He desires a drink, and a jug falls into his hand, and he drinks from it what he wishes, then returns to his place."

The readers (qurrāʾ) differed in their recitation (qirāʾah) of His words: ﴿and in it is whatever the souls desire﴾. The majority of the readers of Madinah and Syria recited ﴿mā tashtahīhi﴾ with an added hāʾ, and likewise it is in their codices (maṣāḥif). The majority of the readers of Iraq recited ﴿tashtahī﴾ without the hāʾ, and likewise it is in their codices.

The correct view regarding this is that they are two well-known recitations with one meaning, so whichever of them the reader recites is correct.

The explanation of His statement, exalted is His remembrance (ta'wil, the interpretation of the Qur'an's meaning):

﴿And that is the Garden which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do.﴾ ﴿For you therein is abundant fruit, from which you will eat.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: It will be said to them, "This is the Garden which God has given you as an inheritance from the people of the Fire, whom He caused to enter Jahannam, because of the good deeds you used to do in the world."

﴿For you therein﴾ means: For you in the Garden is abundant fruit of every kind. ﴿From which you will eat﴾ means: From the fruit you will eat whatever you desire.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verses 74–76:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the criminals will abide in the punishment of Hell forever. It will not be lightened for them, and they will be in it in despair. And We did not wrong them, but they were [themselves] the wrongdoers.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the criminals﴾, who committed the crime of disbelief in God in this world, and so they committed it in the Hereafter as well, ﴿will abide in the punishment of Hell forever﴾, meaning: they will remain in it permanently.

﴿It will not be lightened for them﴾, meaning: the punishment will not be eased for them. The root of fatr is weakness. ﴿And they will be in it in despair﴾, meaning: they will be in the punishment of Hell in despair, and the pronoun in fihi refers to the punishment. It is reported that in the recitation of Abdullah it reads: "wa hum fiha mublisun" ("and they will be in it in despair"), and the meaning is: they will be in Hell in despair. The mublis (one in despair) in this context is the one who has despaired of salvation, who has given up and submitted to the punishment and affliction.

Those of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Of those who said so:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and they will be in it in despair﴾: meaning, submitting.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿and they will be in it in despair﴾, he said: despairing.

Others said something different:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿and they will be in it in despair﴾: their condition will have changed.

We have already explained the meaning of ibsal (despair) with its evidences earlier, and mentioned those who differed about it, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary in this place.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verses 77–78:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And they will call out, "O Malik (the keeper of Hell), let your Lord put an end to us!" He will say, "Indeed, you will remain [here forever]." (77) Certainly We brought you the truth, but most of you are averse to the truth.﴾ (78)

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 43, verses 81–82:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers."﴾ (81) ﴿Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.﴾ (82)

The interpreters of the Qur'an differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say: "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers."﴾ Some of them said: The meaning of that is: Say, O Muhammad, "If the Most Merciful has a son, as you claim and assert, O polytheists, then I am the first of the believers in God in denying you, and in rejecting what you have said, that He has a son."

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Say: "If the Most Merciful had a son"﴾ as you say, ﴿then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾, the believers in God; so say whatever you wish.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾, he said: Say, "If God had a son according to your claim, then I would be the first to worship God, to declare Him one, and to deny you."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Say, "There was never a son for the Most Merciful, so I am the first of those who worship Him in this regard."

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿Say: "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers."﴾ He says: "The Most Merciful had no son, so I am the first of the witnesses."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is negation, and the meaning of "in" (in) is denial; its interpretation is: "That never was, and it is not fitting that it should be."

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿Say: "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers."﴾ Qatadah said: "This is an expression from the speech of the Arabs: ﴿If the Most Merciful had a son﴾: that is, that never occurred and it is not fitting."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿Say: "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers."﴾ He said: "This is al-Inkaf [[In al-Nihayah by Ibn al-Athir: inkaf Allah min su': that is, His glorification and sanctification. And ankafahu: he declared him free of it.]] — 'the Most Merciful never had a son'; God is exonerated from having a son. The 'ma' is only: 'the Most Merciful never had a son, He has no son,' like His saying: ﴿And indeed their plotting was such that the mountains might be moved by it﴾; it is only: 'their plotting was not such that the mountains would be moved by it'; so what God has sent down in His Book and decreed of His decree is firmer than the mountains. And 'in' is 'ma': 'in kana ma kana' — the Arabs say: 'in kana' and 'ma kana' which is said. And in His saying: ﴿then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾, the first who worships God by faith and affirmation that the Most Merciful has no son — on this I worship God."

Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, saying: I asked Ibn Muhammad about the saying of God: ﴿If the Most Merciful had a son﴾; he said: "Ma kana" (it never was).

Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: I asked Zayd ibn Aslam about the saying of God: ﴿Say: "If the Most Merciful had a son"﴾; he said: "This is a well-known expression of the Arabs: 'in kana' means 'ma kana' — 'in kana hadha al-amr qatt' (if this matter ever was)." Then he said: "And His saying: 'in kana' means 'ma kana'."

Others said: The meaning of "in" in this place is the meaning of conditional (al-mujazah), and they said: The interpretation of the speech is: "If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first to worship Him on that basis."

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿Say: "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers."﴾ He said: "If He had a son, I would be the first to worship Him as having a son, but He has no son."

Others said: The meaning of that is: Say, "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of those who refuse (anafin) that." They directed the meaning of "worshippers" to "those who deny and refuse," from the saying of the Arabs: "So-and-so was offended (abida) by this matter" when he was disdainful of it, angry at it, and refused it; so he is "ya'badu abadan," as the poet said:

Alas, Umm al-Walid has fallen in love, and has become, because of what she saw in my head, "ta'abbadu" [[This is a witness whose speaker I have not identified. The author cited it at His saying: (fa-ana awwalu al-'abidin). Abu Ubaydah said in his explanation of the verse (Majaz al-Qur'an, folio 221): its majaz (figurative sense) is "if the Most Merciful had a son": "in" stands in place of "ma" in the saying of some: "ma kana li-l-Rahman walad." And "fa" has the sense of "wa." He means: "ma kana, wa ana awwal al-'abidin."

Others said: Its majaz is: "If in your claim the Most Merciful had a son, then I am the first of the worshippers," that is, the disbelievers in that and the deniers of what you have said. It derives from 'abidtu ta'badu (one is disdainful), i.e., in the pattern of 'alima ya'lamu. It means "to be offended, angry, or to dislike a thing." In the verse "ta'abbadu" means "she is offended or angry," and it is like "abida" in the sense of "to be offended and angry," as stated in Lisan al-Arab (root: '-b-d): "ta'abbada: like 'abida."]]

And as the other said:

"Whenever a lover wishes, he will sever his friend, and he will be disdainful toward him and will inevitably be unjust [[This is also a witness whose speaker I have not identified, and it has the same meaning as the preceding witness. The author cited it on the verse itself, meaning that the poet's words "ya'bad 'alayhi" (he is disdainful toward him) is the present tense of "'abida 'alayhi" in the pattern of "'alima," i.e., to become angry with him. In Lisan al-Arab (root: '-b-d): "al-'abad" (in the pattern of "sabab") means prolonged anger. Al-Farra said: "'abida 'alayhi" and "ahanna 'alayhi" mean he was angry. Al-Ghanawi said: "al-'abad" means grief and passion. Al-Farazdaq said: 'Those are my people; if you satirize them, I satirize them, and I am disdainful to satirize Kulayb with Darim.' "A'bad": i.e., "ana f" (I am offended). End.]]

And Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to me, from Abu Qasit, from Bujah ibn Zayd al-Juhani, that a woman from among them entered upon her husband, who was also a man from among them, and she gave birth to a child for him after six months. This was mentioned to Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), who ordered her to be stoned. Then Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) entered upon him and said: "Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, says in His Book: ﴿And his carrying and his weaning is thirty months﴾ and He says: ﴿And his weaning is in two years﴾." He said: "By Allah, Uthman was not disdainful until he sent for her to be returned." Yunus said, Ibn Wahb said: "'Abida" means "istankafa" (he refused/was offended).

The most correct of the sayings in this matter, in my view, is the saying of those who said: the meaning of "in" is the conditional that requires a consequent, as we have mentioned from al-Suddi. This is because "in" in this place can only have one of two meanings: either it is the particle meaning the condition that calls for a consequent, or it is in the sense of denial. But if it is directed toward denial, the speech would not have great meaning, since it would become: "Say: 'The Most Merciful never had a son.'" And when it takes that meaning, it would mislead the ignorant among the polytheists into thinking that He only denied that God, mighty and majestic, had a son at some earlier time, and then a son came into being for Him after there was none — even though, if that were its meaning, those to whom God commanded His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to say, "The Most Merciful never had a son, so I am the first of the worshippers," would say to him, "You have spoken the truth, it is as you said; we do not claim that He has always had a son. We only say that He had no son, then He created the jinn and became related to them by marriage, and a son came to be for Him from them," as God has informed us that they used to say. God, may His remembrance be exalted, would not have argued for His Prophet ﷺ and against his deniers with a proof that they could challenge. Since directing "in" to the sense of denial has the problems we have mentioned, the meaning closest to it is the conditional. Since that is so, the clear proof of the correctness of what we say — that the meaning of the speech is: "Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people who claim that the angels are daughters of God: 'If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first among you to worship Him in that way, but He has no son, so I worship Him in that He has no son, and it is not fitting that He should have one.'"

When the speech is directed to what we have said in this manner, it is not in the form of doubt, but in the form of gentle address and good discourse, as His saying, glorified is His praise: ﴿Say: "Indeed God, or we or you are upon guidance or in clear error."﴾ And He knows that the truth is with Him and that His opponents are in clear error.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verses 83–84:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So leave them to plunge into vain talk and to play, until they encounter their Day which they are promised﴾ [43:83] ﴿And He is the One who is God in the heaven and God on the earth. And He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing﴾ [43:84]

The Exalted says: So leave them, O Muhammad, these liars against God who attribute to Him a son, to plunge into their falsehood and to play in their worldly life, ﴿until they encounter their Day which they are promised﴾, and that is the day on which God will cast them into Hell because of their slander against Him, and it is the Day of Resurrection.

As related by:

* Muhammad narrated to us, who said: Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿until they encounter their Day which they are promised﴾: He said: It is the Day of Resurrection.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And He is the One who is God in the heaven and God on the earth﴾

The Exalted says: God, to whom belongs divinity, is worshipped in the heaven and worshipped on the earth, just as He is worshipped in the heaven; there is nothing other than Him whose worship is fitting. The Exalted means: So single out for worship the One who has this attribute, and do not associate anything else with Him.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said regarding this.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned﴾ (85)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Blessed is He who has authority over the seven heavens and the earth and what is between them of all things; His judgment prevails over all of that, and His decree is executed over them. He says: How, then, could there be for Him a partner, when the one who is in His authority and under His rule has no power against Him? ﴿And with Him is the knowledge of the Hour﴾ means: with Him is the knowledge of the Hour in which the Resurrection occurs and creation is gathered from their graves to the place of reckoning.

He says: And to Him, O people, you will be returned after your deaths, and you will come to Him, and He will recompense the one who does good for his good and the one who does evil for his evil.

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And those whom they invoke besides Him have no power of intercession, except those who testify to the truth while they know﴾ (86)

The people of interpretation differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: Jesus, Ezra and the angels, whom these polytheists worship, do not possess intercession with God for anyone, except those who testify to the truth, meaning those who affirm the oneness of God and obey Him, with a knowledge of it and a sound acceptance of what His messengers brought.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿And those whom they invoke besides Him have no power of intercession﴾ he said: 'Isa, 'Uzayr, and the angels.

* *

His saying: ﴿except those who testify to the truth﴾

He said: the word of sincerity (kalimat al-ikhlas), and they know that God is the Truth. Jesus, Ezra and the angels say: Jesus, Ezra and the angels will not intercede except for those who testify to the truth, while knowing the truth.

Others said: What is meant by that is: the deities that the polytheists invoke and worship besides God do not possess intercession, except Jesus, Ezra and their kin, and the angels, who testified to the truth, acknowledging it, while knowing the reality of what they testified to.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And those whom they invoke besides Him have no power of intercession, except those who testify to the truth while they know﴾: the angels, Jesus and Ezra, who have been worshipped besides God, and they have intercession with God and a station.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿except those who testify to the truth﴾ he said: the angels, Jesus son of Mary and Ezra, for they have testimony with God.

The most correct of these sayings, in terms of truth, is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed that those whom the polytheists worship besides God do not possess intercession with Him for anyone, except those who testify to the truth. Their testimony to the truth is their affirmation of God's oneness, meaning: except those who believe in God while knowing the reality of His oneness. He did not specify that those among them who do not possess intercession are some of those worshipped besides God; rather, it applies to all whom the Quraysh worshipped besides God on the day this verse was revealed, and others. Among them were those who worshipped deities besides God, and among them were those who worshipped angels and others besides Him. All of those are included in His saying: those whom Quraysh and the rest of the Arabs invoke besides God have no power of intercession with God. Then He, may His praise be exalted, made an exception with His saying: ﴿except those who testify to the truth while they know﴾, and they are those who bear true witness, affirming God's oneness and sincerely devoting oneness to Him, with knowledge and certainty of that, that they possess intercession with Him by His permission for them to do so, as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And they do not intercede except for whom He approves﴾. Thus He, may His praise be exalted, affirmed for the angels, Jesus and Ezra a possession of intercession which He negated for the idols and images, through the exception He made.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 43, verse 85–86:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned﴾ (85)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Blessed is He who has authority over the seven heavens and the earth and what is between them of all things; His judgment prevails over all of that, and His decree is executed over them. He says: How, then, could there be for Him a partner, when the one who is in His authority and under His rule has no power against Him? ﴿And with Him is the knowledge of the Hour﴾ means: with Him is the knowledge of the Hour in which the Resurrection occurs and creation is gathered from their graves to the place of reckoning.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And if you were to ask them, "Who created them?" they would surely say, "Allah." So how are they turned away?﴾ (87) ﴿And [He knows] his saying, "My Lord, these are a people who do not believe."﴾ (88)

He, the Exalted, says: If you were to ask these polytheists among your people, O Muhammad, "Who created them?" they would surely say, "Allah created us."

﴿So how are they turned away?﴾ In what manner are they diverted from worshipping the One who created them, and deprived of reaching the truth in His worship?

* *

As for His words: ﴿And [He knows] his saying, "My Lord, these are a people who do not believe."﴾

The reciters differed over the recitation of His words ﴿wa-qīlihi﴾. The majority of the reciters of Madina, Makka and Basra recited it as "wa-qīlahu" with a fatḥa (naṣb, the accusative case). When it is read this way, it has two possible interpretations. The first is that it is coordinated (ʿaṭf) with His words: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private conversation?﴾, meaning, "and We hear his saying, 'My Lord.'" The second is that a verb is implied for it, so the meaning becomes: "and he said his saying, 'My Lord, these are a people who do not believe,' and Muhammad complained of his grievance to his Lord." The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited ﴿wa-qīlihi﴾ with a kasra (khafḍ, the genitive case), meaning: "and with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and the knowledge of his saying."

The correct view on this matter is that both are well-known recitations of the major cities, and both are sound in meaning, so whichever one the reciter reads is correct. The meaning of the speech therefore is: Muhammad said his saying, complaining to his Lord, may He be blessed and exalted, about his people who denied him and about what he suffered from them: "My Lord, these are the people to whom You sent me to warn and whom You commanded me to call to You; they are a people who do not believe."

The discussion on the interpretation (*ta'wil*, the explanation of a Qur'anic text's meaning) of the words of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿So overlook them, and say, "Peace," for they will come to know﴾ (89).

His Exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), in response to his supplication when he said, "My Lord, these are a people who do not believe": ﴿So overlook them﴾, O Muhammad, and turn away from their harm. ﴿And say﴾ to them, ﴿"Peace"﴾, meaning "Peace be upon you." The word *salam* (peace) is in the nominative case (*raf'*) by an implied pronoun in *'alaykum* (upon you) or *lakum* (for you).

The reciters differed over the recitation of His words ﴿fa-sawfa ya'lamun (they will come to know)﴾. Most of the reciters of Madina recited it as *fa-sawfa ta'lamun* with the *ta'* (second person, "you will come to know"), meaning that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to say that to the polytheists, following His words *"Peace."* Most of the reciters of Kufa and some of the reciters of Makka recited it as *fa-sawfa ya'lamun* with the *ya'* (third person, "they will come to know"), as a statement, and as a threat from Allah to the polytheists. Its interpretation according to this recitation is: ﴿So overlook them﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿and say, "Peace."﴾ Then His Exalted remembrance began the threat against them, saying ﴿they will come to know﴾ what afflictions, punishments and torment they will meet because of their disbelief. Then Allah, Mighty is His praise, abrogated (*naskh*, the cancellation of a ruling by a later revelation) this verse and commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to fight them.

As related:

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, concerning ﴿So overlook them and say, "Peace"﴾: He said, "Overlook them, then He commanded him to fight them."

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, who said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, consoles His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿So overlook them and say, "Peace," for they will come to know.﴾

End of the commentary on Surat al-Zukhruf.
